podcast.title: Connection with Marilyn Manson
podcast.body: Through an indirect route, Jan Terry connected with Marilyn Manson, who became a fan. Manson hired her to sing at his birthday party, and she subsequently opened a series of shows for him. "Through a roundabout way, she connected with Marilyn Manson, who loved her so much, that he hired her to sing at his birthday party."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Musical Background
podcast.body: Jan Terry, described by IMDb as an "endearingly bad amateur Italian American singer-songwriter" and topping out at about five feet, was originally from Chicago. She played in a jug band with her parents, where all three performed Elvis covers in blackface. "She was originally from Chicago, where she played in a jug band with her mom and dad. All three would perform Elvis covers in blackface."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Internet Presence
podcast.body: In the internet age, her music became accessible to a wider audience, allowing everyone to enjoy her unique style. "Now that we're in the internet age, everyone can enjoy Jan's music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Music Videos and Self-Promotion
podcast.body: Despite her day job, she never abandoned her musical aspirations. She began recording songs and producing music videos, which she distributed to her limo passengers on VHS tapes. "She started recording songs and making music videos, which she put on VHS tapes that were handed out to her limo passengers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Outsider Music Hero
podcast.body: Jan Terry is regarded as an outsider music hero by many. "Jan Terry, an outsider music and hero to many."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Professional Music Training and Day Jobs
podcast.body: She pursued a legitimate career path in the music business, earning a certificate in sound engineering and occasionally working as a backup singer. When that didn't work out, she became a limo driver. "Jan started a legitimate career in the music business, earning a certificate in sound engineering, and also serving as the occasional backup singer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
